summary.text: A 34-year-old woman developed persistent right aural fullness after septoplasty, with conductive hearing loss, tympanic membrane perforation and recurrent otorrhea unresponsive to standard and antibiotic treatment.

Facial nerve palsy (House-Brackmann grade IV) recovered with hospital treatment, then recurred two weeks after canal wall-up antromastoidectomy and progressed from grade II to grade V; the first operation showed only necrosis.

Re-antromastoidectomy histopathology, Ziehl-Neelsen staining, ear smear and culture established tuberculous otitis media (susceptible Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex); she received 3HRZE/9HR, extended because AFB persisted on swabs.

Sequelae were an external auditory canal skin defect, mesotympanic perforation, grade IV facial palsy and profound right hearing loss, with ongoing non-tuberculous otorrhea and petrosectomy under consideration.

summary.text: A 29-year-old woman in her fourth week of pregnancy presented with nasal obstruction and persistent aural fullness after an upper respiratory tract infection; middle-ear effusion was found and myringotomy cultured Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with local improvement on topical ciprofloxacin.

Right otorrhea recurred, followed by sinusitis and left acute otitis media; Streptococcus pneumoniae grew from the right ear, a sinus puncture and left ventilation tube were done, cultures became sterile on systemic therapy, then a productive cough developed.

Because her father and brother had pulmonary tuberculosis, evaluation found AFB on sputum smear with Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex on molecular testing and culture; 2HRZE/4HR was started, she delivered a full-term infant with non-tuberculous congenital pneumonia, and symptoms gradually resolved.

Sequelae were bilateral subtotal tympanic membrane perforations with conductive hearing loss of about 40 dB HL, five myringoplasties with persisting small perforations, and no tuberculosis recurrence over nearly a decade.

summary.text: A 19-year-old woman with no significant medical history developed right aural fullness and conductive hearing loss after intensive nasal irrigation for rhinosinusitis; Eustachian tube treatment and empirical antibiotics did not help, and work-up showed a type B tympanogram, 40 dB conductive loss and opacified middle ear and mastoid on HRCT.

Nine months after symptom onset she had right canal wall-up antromastoidectomy, followed about three weeks later by peripheral facial palsy (House-Brackmann grade IV), re-hospitalization and revision surgery.

Caseous granulation tissue with caseating necrosis, Ziehl-Neelsen AFB, molecular testing and culture identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex; she received 2HRZE/4HR, facial palsy gradually resolved and a postauricular fistula developed.
Three months after completing therapy she had fistula closure with tympanic membrane reconstruction; facial function improved to grade II but severe mixed hearing loss persisted.
